name: mason_dixon_resurvey
one_line: Replay a finished, accepted task at lower cost and compare the two bills.
problem: Waste that no per-cause share can show: a whole task done in a heavier way than needed (model tier, context size, number of agents).
design: Pick a finished task whose accepted output and Hamilton profile are committed (e.g. one PR merge or one X1 phase).
Replay it from its starting commit with one change at a time (smaller model for routine steps, fresh session at each phase, no standing monitors), in a scratch branch that is never merged.
Compare the replay's get_session cost and checker result with the original's; the replay is the 'after' arm and the audited original is the 'before' arm of an add-test record.
Emit the winning change as a saver candidate, with the measured pair attached as its first test.

cost_estimate.basis: build is about one agent session; each replay costs roughly 25-60% of the original task (the original PR-merge session cost $4.97, the X1 coordinator $38.82)
cost_estimate.note: Estimate only (unverified). Never counted as a saving.

first_test: Replay the PR-merge task (about $5 original) once with phase handoff on.
risks: Replays can drift from the original task; the checker must be the same one. Costs real money before it saves any.
